terminal

ejm-cli stays light.

A coding agent for your terminal. One native Rust binary, read only until you grant more, built to run a hundred sessions without flooding your machine.

Build from source How it works

how it works

Built for the terminal you already use.

The screen follows your terminal colors and never paints a background. --replay is an offline demo provider, so you can try it with no account and no network.

A real composer

Unicode, multiline input, bracketed paste and message history. Paste a stack trace without sending it by accident.

Readable streaming

Code, Markdown and diffs are styled as they arrive. Control sequences in model and tool output are stripped, never run.

Steer mid-run

Queue the next turn, redirect the current one, or stop it. Every run state stays visible.

Saved sessions

Pick up any session by ID or prefix. Durable history lives in the harness, not in your scrollback.

Pipes and scripts

ejm-cli run streams plain text, or one JSON event per line with --json. Failures exit nonzero.

Clean exits

Raw mode, mouse tracking and the alternate screen are restored after errors, signals and panics.

keys

Five keys to remember.

Type /help in the app for the full list of keys and commands.

Main keys in the ejm-cli TUI
KeyAction
EnterSend a turn, or queue it while a run is active
Alt+EnterInsert a newline
Ctrl+KSteer the active run with your draft
Ctrl+SChoose a saved session
Ctrl+CStop the current run, or exit when idle

permissions

You grant every permission.

File tools start read only. Writing and shell access are flags you pass on purpose, and the grants stay visible in the header for the life of the process.

Add access one flag at a time.

Keys come from environment variables and are never accepted as arguments.

warning

Native execution runs as you and is not a sandbox. ejm-cli doctor reports exactly what is enforced.

# read only
ejm-cli

# let it edit files
ejm-cli --allow-write

# and run commands
ejm-cli --allow-write --allow-shell

footprint

Light by design.

No Node or Python runtime. Agents share one resource governor instead of opening a shell each, and rendering memory has a hard ceiling.

managed sessions by default
100
model requests at once by default, with 4 local jobs and 1 heavy job
8
KiB cap on visible transcript memory
256
ms to first composer paint, fresh state
24

note

Paint time measured on 18 October 2026 on a Mac16,8 with a replay provider, from process start to first paint in a real PTY. Warm p95 was 41 ms across 20 samples. A modern Mac does not prove the old-laptop target, and no comparison with other agents has run yet.

models

Bring your own model.

Four provider kinds work today. Pick one with --provider, or pass an explicit model.

Providers and how to use each
ProviderHow to use it
OpenAI compatibleAny Chat Completions endpoint. Set EJM_CLI_BASE_URL and EJM_CLI_MODEL.
OpenAI ResponsesNative Responses access with your API key.
ChatGPTejm-cli login chatgpt signs in through your browser. Tokens never touch arguments, logs or the screen.
AnthropicNative Anthropic API access with an explicit model.

get it

Build ejm-cli from source.

ejm-cli is a v0.1.0 source release and has not been published or packaged yet. It is MIT licensed and Rust only.

  1. Check out the engine

    ejm-cli builds against ejm-harness, checked out as a sibling directory.

  2. Build

    cargo build --release --locked

  3. Try it offline

    ./target/release/ejm-cli --replay

  4. Read the options

    ejm-cli --help lists every command and flag.

questions

Before you try it.

Does it need an account?

No account or server connection is needed. You bring a model through an API key or a ChatGPT sign-in.

Can ejm-cli change my files?

Only if you pass --allow-write or --allow-shell. File tools are read only otherwise, and the grants stay visible on screen.

Is it a sandbox?

No. Native execution runs as the current user. ejm-cli doctor reports which restrictions are enforced.

How do I use it in a script?

Use ejm-cli run. It streams plain text, or one JSON event per line with --json, and failures exit nonzero. The TUI itself needs a terminal.

Does it work without color?

Yes. --no-color or NO_COLOR gives a monochrome screen, and --plain switches to ASCII symbols.

Built on an open engine.

ejm-cli is a separate app on ejm-harness, the Rust engine that runs many sessions through one resource governor.
